notes.title: Patch 1.0.7.0 – UX Rework, Audio Settings, Texture Fixes, & Invert X/Y Option
notes.content:
Hey everyone! After a longer break, we’re back with Update 1.0.7.0, which brings long-requested UX improvements, audio options, visual fixes, and a more dynamic forest environment. Here's what’s new:

✅ New Audio Settings Menu
You can now adjust music, sound effects, and voice volume independently. This updated design offers much better control over your audio experience.

✅ Invert X/Y Axis Options Added
You can now invert the X and Y camera axis in the settings menu — another frequent player request.

✅ Box Puzzle Texture Fix (Low Settings)
Fixed a bug where symbols on the box puzzle were hard to see or completely missing when playing on lower texture quality. The signs should now display clearly. If any issues persist, please report them in the Discussions section.

✅ Animated Forest Environment
The forest is no longer static! We’ve added motion to the trees and leaves, making the environment feel more alive and immersive.

✅ Minor Bug Fixes
A handful of small bugs have been addressed to ensure a smoother gameplay experience.

🔜 Coming Next
🎧 Sound Designer Wanted
We’re currently searching for a talented sound designer to help us elevate the game’s overall audio feel.

🎮 Gamepad Support (80% Complete)
Full controller support is nearly done and should be ready in the next update.

🌿 UI & Vegetation Visual Rework (In Planning)
We’re exploring a full visual refresh of the in-game UI and vegetation layout to improve aesthetics and readability.

Thanks for supporting Code Alkonost! As always, your feedback helps shape the game — feel free to post suggestions or report bugs in the community.

Stay safe, and don’t trust the silence in the woods... 🌑

— Alkonost Team

notes.title: Devlog #1 – The Origin of Code Alkonost: From Detective Noir to Slavic Descent
notes.content:
Every game has an origin story, and Code Alkonost: Awakening of Evil is no exception. In fact, the journey of creating this game took more than a few unexpected twists. In this first developer blog, we want to share how our initial idea morphed into the game you know today. It’s a tale of ambition, setback, reinvention, and ultimately, perseverance. We’ll pull back the curtain on our project’s early days back when it wasn’t even called Code Alkonost and reflect on how those experiences shaped the adventure that Awakening of Evil became. We hope this candid look at our development journey inspires you and gives you a deeper appreciation for the world you’re exploring in the game.


Code Gamyun – Detective Noir Meets Slavic Mythology (2022)
Back in 2022, our team embarked on an earlier incarnation of this project, then code-named “Code Gamyun” The name itself was a nod to Slavic mythology, reflecting the cultural roots we wanted to explore.

Our concept was ambitious: imagine a noir-style private detective plunging into a mythological Slavic underworld. This protagonist was heavily inspired by Leon S. Kennedy from Resident Evil – a seasoned, sharp-witted investigator type, but facing otherworldly horrors instead of zombies. By his side journeyed a fierce Slavic warrior woman reminiscent of Ciri from The Witcher, wielding medieval weaponry and ancient knowledge.

It was an unlikely duo we adored: the modern detective and the ancient warrior, teaming up against the darkness.

Early Concept Art – The Detective & The Warrior: This artwork from the Code Gamyun era shows our original protagonists in a dark, atmospheric style. The brooding detective (left) brandishes a handgun, clad in a long coat and determination, while his companion – a battle-hardened Slavic huntress (right) – stands ready with her axe. We envisioned them descending into torch-lit catacombs and misty forests beneath the mundane world, confronting nightmarish creatures from Slavic folklore.

The tone at this stage was very much action-adventure: tense shootouts with demonic foes, close-quarters combat alongside dialogue choices, and a series of boss fights against legendary underworld guardians. This early vision was cinematic and intense, blending detective noir with mythological fantasy in a way we hadn’t seen before.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42595694/05e13f2c810e3d3cd79933a496ed7801da8ba70a.png
Code Gamayun - Main Characters

A Promising Start – Pitching the Vision and Early Support
With a clear concept and palpable enthusiasm, we moved forward to pitch the Code Gamyun project to potential supporters. By late 2022, we compiled concept art, a storyline overview, and gameplay prototypes to present our idea for funding. Excitingly, we earned an early approval from a Innovation fund. Getting financial support felt incredible – it was validation that our crazy detective-meets-folklore idea had real promise. We remember the day we got the news; there was joy, relief, and an overwhelming surge of motivation.

Early funding meant we could start expanding the project properly: build more prototypes, refine the art, and perhaps most importantly, work with confidence that the game had backing. It’s hard to overstate what that support did for team morale. We started planning out full production for the coming year – scheduling content creation, level design, and all those boss encounters we had dreamed up. Our small indie team was on cloud nine, fueled by the encouragement from the funding committee and our own creative drive. In hindsight, that period was a golden time of optimism where everything seemed possible.

Crisis Point – Losing Key Team Members and Funding
Game development is rarely a smooth ride, and for us a major crisis hit in 2023 just as things were gearing up.

Two of our core team members left the project: our lead environmental artist and our tech lead. These weren’t just any teammates; they were pivotal to realizing the vision. The environmental artist was the one who could bring those eerie Slavic underworld landscapes to life, and the tech lead was the backbone holding the code together. Their departure was a heavy blow to our small team. We found ourselves suddenly without the architect of our world’s atmosphere and the guide of our technical implementation.
To make matters worse, the creative fund that had approved us did so based on our original team lineup. When we informed them of the changes, they declined to accept the new team composition. In their eyes, our project had fundamentally changed; the expertise they’d trusted to deliver this game was no longer all on board. As a result, the previously awarded funding was revoked. That was a heartbreaking moment. We understood the fund’s position – it’s standard procedure, after all – but it felt like the rug had been pulled out from under us. Months of work and planning were suddenly in jeopardy. We were left reeling, faced with an uncomfortable question: What now?
For a while, we were truly at a crossroads. Do we try to replace those team members quickly and press on with the same concept, essentially attempting to rebuild the project mid-stream? Or do we accept this setback as a sign to rethink our approach entirely? It was an emotionally charged period. We had tough meetings, candid heart-to-heart discussions, and more than a few sleepless nights pondering the fate of Code Gamyun. It’s in these moments that a team’s resilience is tested. Despite the pain of seeing our original vision crumble, a spark of determination remained. We weren’t ready to give up on making a game rooted in Slavic myth – but maybe, we realized, the game we ultimately make didn’t have to be the one we first imagined.

Reinventing the Game – From Code Gamyun to Code Alkonost
Ultimately, we chose not to try resurrecting Code Gamyun as it was. Instead, we decided to reinvent the project from the ground up. This was not a light decision; it meant scrapping or reworking a lot of what we had built so far. But starting fresh also felt liberating in a strange way. We gathered the remaining team and had an honest conversation: What if we created a different game using the knowledge and passion we gained, but scoped to what our new smaller team could achieve, and more aligned with the mood we wanted to convey? The answer to that question became the foundation of our rebooted project, which we renamed Code Alkonost.
One of the first big changes was the protagonist. We moved away from the hardened male detective archetype and introduced Vera as the new lead. Vera is a young woman drawn into the darkness of Slavic legends, and unlike a grizzled detective, she isn’t equipped to charge in guns blazing. In fact, we removed guns entirely from the design. This was a deliberate pivot to make the player feel more vulnerable and to shift the gameplay focus. Vera’s strength would come from her courage, intuition, and resilience – not from firearms or brute force. This immediately gave the game a more survival vibe, which we found both challenging and exciting. We started asking ourselves what truly makes something scary or unsettling, beyond jump scares or action. The answers we landed on guided the new direction of the game.
Along with Vera’s introduction came a tone shift. We leaned heavily into dark fantasy and atmospheric tension. Instead of facing hordes of enemies with an ally at your back, the player (as Vera) often finds themselves alone in creepy, otherworldly places, with the feeling that something isn’t quite right. We drew inspiration from classics like Silent Hill and Amnesia for creating dread through environment and story, rather than firefights. The narrative became more personal and introspective – Vera’s descent is as much about confronting inner demons as it is about dealing with literal demons of folklore. This new approach allowed us to explore themes of symbolism and morality in Slavic myths on a deeper level. Every creature or supernatural event in Code Alkonost now had a meaning behind it, a riddle to unravel, or a lesson for Vera to learn, which made the writing process far more enriching.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42595694/706fb1f452134eca435416ad037eda4b129b203b.jpg
Vera - an ordinary housewife, suddenly wakes up in a surreal, alternate world

From Action to Introspection – Embracing Puzzles and Folklore
Shifting away from action gameplay, we needed new core mechanics to engage players. The answer was found in the rich puzzle-solving traditions of adventure games, now intertwined with Slavic folklore elements. We designed puzzles that would make players think and feel the lore rather than just witness it. Instead of dodging attacks and returning fire, you might be deciphering ancient Cyrillic runes, mixing traditional herbs for a ritual, or arranging symbolic artifacts to appease a restless spirit. Our goal was to have the gameplay itself tell part of the story.

Folklore Puzzle Interface: Here is an example of the kind of puzzle players face in Code Alkonost. Rather than a gunfight, you’re presented with a task steeped in symbolism – in this case, combining elemental icons in the correct way to unlock a ritual or mechanism.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42595694/6cccc016acaf9b4d8e467efda1ebcf4f7b0f8119.gif
Crafting Puzzle

This interface illustrates our puzzle-centric design: it’s clean but cryptic, forcing you to ponder the relationships between natural elements. Each symbol and combination in the game has roots in Slavic myth. By solving these puzzles, players aren’t just progressing in the game; they’re also learning the logic of the folklore in Vera’s world. We found this approach creates a different kind of tension and reward. It’s not about fast reflexes, but patience, observation, and understanding – a cerebral challenge that can be just as thrilling, especially when the solution reveals a new story twist or a haunting piece of lore.

Of course, puzzles are just one aspect of the new gameplay. Exploration and discovery became equally important. Without combat, the player’s main interactions involve searching environments for clues, tools, and story bits. We revamped the inventory and interaction systems to support this scavenging style of play. Every item you pick up might help you survive the next encounter in a non-traditional way. The absence of weapons meant we had to get creative with obstacles and how the player overcomes them, often leaning on superstition and clever use of the environment.

Collecting Folklore Artifacts: Instead of ammo and guns, Vera’s world is filled with mystical items and clues to collect, as shown in the inventory interface above. Berries, herbs, strange tokens, ritual tools – these are the kinds of objects you gather and use. In this screenshot, you can see examples like berries and a wooden bucket, which might be ingredients for a folkloric recipe or offerings to otherworldly beings. The UI we designed highlights a symbolic wheel behind the grid, reinforcing that every item has a place in some greater ritual or puzzle. This shift in gameplay drastically changed the feel of the project. It slowed the pace in a good way – encouraging players to soak in the atmosphere, read notes, examine carvings, and truly immerse themselves in the storytelling. We traded the adrenaline of combat for the slow-burning suspense of not knowing what lurks around the next corner or how you’ll deal with it when it appears. And when danger does strike, Vera must rely on wit or a well-prepared plan to survive. This makes every victory feel earned and every escape from evil feel like a sigh of relief.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42595694/4aea6bdb3ffcaa10e5380d655e3fd00b50defd77.png
Inventory Items

Looking Back – Reflections and Gratitude
By mid-2023, it was clear that our radical pivot had given birth to something special. The game was now living up to the Alkonost name – in Slavic myth, the Alkonost is a mystical bird whose songs can induce either bliss or despair.

Likewise, our game now aimed to evoke a mix of emotions: wonder at the beautiful, eerie world and its legends, and dread at the evils slithering in the shadows. We had transformed a setback into an opportunity to craft a more original experience. It’s not the game we first set out to make, but we believe it’s a better one for having the soul of our struggles poured into it.

Now, standing on the other side of this turbulent development journey, we feel a profound sense of gratitude. It’s almost poetic – the mythical Alkonost rising from the ashes of our earlier project. The road here was not easy. We had to let go of ideas we were deeply attached to and watch an earlier dream fade. But in doing so, we found a new dream that was worth fighting for. In retrospect, losing our funding and original concept was a disguised blessing. It forced us to dig deeper creatively and personally, to ask why we were making this game and what we truly wanted to say with it. The result is a game that is more intimate, distinctive, and, we hope, more impactful for players.
Throughout this process, we learned the value of adaptability and trust. Adaptability, in that we as developers must be willing to change course when fate demands it. And trust, in that we needed to trust each other as a team – that we could build something great even when the odds were against us. We also want to acknowledge that those who left the project early on still contributed to where we are now; their work laid the groundwork, and their departure set the stage for us to grow in new ways. We harbor no ill will – only thanks for being part of the journey.

Most of all, we want to thank you – the players. Whether you’ve been following us since the early concept days or you just discovered Code Alkonost: Awakening of Evil, your support means the world to us. The fact that people out there are now playing and experiencing this game is the ultimate reward that makes every challenge worth it. Thank you for giving our reimagined vision a chance, for diving into this dark world and embracing its story. Every review, comment, and message we’ve received from the community has lifted our spirits and affirmed that we made the right choice in continuing on.


As we share this origin story in Devlog #1, we’re humbled by how far the project has come. From detective noir action to dark fantasy adventure – what a ride! We hope this behind-the-scenes look provides context and meaning to your experience with the game.

We’re excited to continue supporting Awakening of Evil and to share more devlogs exploring everything from our artistic process to the deep cultural roots behind the narrative. There’s so much more we want to talk about and we’re just getting started.

🔜 Up next:

Devlog #2 – David vs. Goliaths
How Code Alkonost outshined million-dollar productions with less than €50,000.

Devlog #3 – Is Code Alkonost a Meta-Narrative Game?
Hidden layers, secrets, and how folklore and narrative loops shape a deeper player experience.

Stay tuned and thank you for being part of this journey. 👁️🕯️

notes.title: What's Next for Code Alkonost: Awakening of Evil?
notes.content:
Thank you to everyone who has played, shared feedback, and supported Code Alkonost so far.
Your response has been incredibly helpful — and we're excited to share what’s coming next.

🗺️ Roadmap Coming Soon – Built on Community Feedback
We’ve been listening closely to players, and we’re using that feedback to shape the future of the game.
Over the coming weeks, we’ll be releasing a detailed roadmap outlining planned updates and improvements — including new puzzles, lore content, and an early preview of our next major narrative chapter.

notes.title: Patch 1.0.6.0 – Bug Fixes & Visual Improvements!
notes.content:
Hey everyone! We’ve just released Patch 1.0.6.0, bringing important fixes and improvements to your experience in Code Alkonost. Here’s what’s new:

✅ Restored Flame Effects – No more missing flames! The fiery atmosphere is back.
✅ Fixed World Map Activation – The world map now properly loads without issues.
✅ Improved FPS Stability – If AI scaling is off, FPS is now locked to 60 FPS for smoother performance.
✅ Other Minor Bug Fixes – Additional tweaks for a better experience.

Thanks for your support! Let us know if you spot anything else. 🔥

notes.title: Update 1.0.5.0 – New Languages, Game Modes & Fixes!
notes.content:
Greetings, players!

We’re excited to bring you Update 1.0.5.0, packed with new language support, gameplay modes, and performance improvements. Here’s what’s new:

🔹 New Language Subtitles
We’ve added subtitle support for German, French, Italian, Spanish, Japanese, and Chinese! Now more players can enjoy the story in their native language.

🎮 Two Gameplay Modes
Modern Mode – Standard gameplay experience with guided hints and assistance.
Old-School Mode – No hints, no guidance! You’ll need to rely on your own logic and observation to solve puzzles and master mechanics. A true test of skill!

⚙️ Performance & Fixes
Fixed frame drops during boss fights, ensuring smoother gameplay.
Restored foliage in several levels that was previously removed due to technical issues, bringing back the original atmosphere.
We appreciate your support and feedback! Let us know how you like the new features.

⚔️ Good luck, and enjoy the game!

notes.title: New Update 1.0.4.0 Released
notes.content:
We've fixed the major FPS drop affecting mid-range and low-end systems. Now, enjoy 60fps (up to 200fps with DLSS).
We apologize for the delay—if you returned the game due to these issues, email your purchase confirmation to codealkonost@gmail.com for a free copy.

notes.title: Patch 1.0.3.0 is Live!
notes.content:
Dear players,

We’ve just released Patch 1.0.3.0, bringing fixes, improvements, and new content based on your feedback!

Fixes:
- Glitches with torches, inscriptions, and candles not emitting light have been resolved.
- Vegetation rendering issues have been addressed.
- Audio problems reported by players have been fixed.
Improvements:
- New settings options for displaying player hints.
- Improved visibility of interactive items.
- New music tracks by Alkonost Band added to enrich the atmosphere.
Localization:
- UI has been translated into Serbian and Russian.
(Tutorials will be finalized and improved in the next updates.)

Performance Tips
If you experience performance issues, we recommend:
- Disable shadow settings.
- Switching to DirectX mode for better performance.

Technical Support:
While the game has been tested on over 20 different hardware configurations, we understand issues can still arise.
If you encounter any technical problems, please reach out to us – your feedback is crucial in helping us improve the experience for everyone.

What’s Next?
Our next update will introduce a game launcher, allowing you to configure settings directly from within the game, without needing to adjust them via Steam.

Thank you for your support and feedback – we are listening!

Alkonost Team

notes.title: First Update – Improvements Based on Your Feedback!
notes.content:
Dear players,

Thank you for supporting and playing Code Alkonost from day one! Your feedback has been incredibly valuable, and we’re excited to bring you our first major update, packed with improvements.

What’s New in This Update?
1. Gameplay Fixes and a New Tutorial
We’ve refined key gameplay mechanics to make the experience more intuitive and enjoyable. Additionally, we’ve added a detailed tutorial to help new players get started quickly and dive into the world of Code Alkonost with ease.

2. Level Design Improvements
Our level design has been polished to enhance the overall experience. We’ve added more detail, optimized transitions, and addressed issues affecting the flow of gameplay. Your adventures are now smoother and more immersive than ever!

3. Optimization for DirectX, Vulkan, and Steam Deck
This update includes major performance optimizations, ensuring a smoother experience on a wider range of devices. We’ve also worked specifically on Steam Deck compatibility, so you can now enjoy Code Alkonost on the go!

4. Achievements Fixed
We’ve resolved all issues related to achievements. If you’ve been chasing those badges, now’s the perfect time to dive back in and complete your collection!

For those of you who have already explored the world of Code Alkonost, we highly encourage you to give it another go. With these updates, your experience will be better than ever, and you might discover something new!

Thank you again for your support and for being part of our journey. Your feedback fuels our progress, so keep it coming!

Alkonost Team

Psst… ovo je demo igra koja je do 2. novembra na Steamu. Za to vreme, uživajte u igri, dajte nam vaš iskren feedback, iskustva, kritike. A očekuju vas i razna gejming iznenađenja.
To nije sve!!! Iteresuje te AR dizajn? 3D Dizajn objekata i likova? Za vreme Scream Festa organizujemo i konkurs za noajbolju AR horror priču:
Ispričaj svoju horror AR priču
- Koristi dizajnerska i AR okruženja koja su ti najadekvatnija. 
- Kreiraj bića iz Slovenske mitologije. 
- izanimiraj i snimi sam ili sa svojim drugarima horor scene sa temom „osećaj bliske i neposredne opasnosti od onostranih bića“ u realnom okruženju.
- Uploaduj na svom TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, X nalogu sa oznakom @codealkonost
- Osvoji early Access igre i postani deo kreativnog Alkonost tima.
Opis: Code Alkonost je avanturistička igra iz prvog lica bogata pričama i atmosferom inspirisana slovenskom mitologijom. Putujte kroz mračni svet fantazije i naiđite na posesivne duhove i iluzije podzemlja. Doživite autentični umetnički stil i priče koje nikada ranije nisu viđene u avanturističkim igrama.
Alkonost tim vas poziva da učestvujete na Scream Fest i isprobate demo verziju igre: https://store.steampowered.com/app/2062030/Code_Alkonost_Awakening_of_Evil/

notes.title: Code Alkonost Showcase video
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42595694/9a5bb54349a56991532ca68ffc4621e300c66fa3.png

Remote Human is excited to relevel new details for the upcoming single-player adventure survival-horror game Code Alkonost. The showcase presentation revealed details from the early stages of the development and includes game story details, game mechanics, game environments, concept art, a sample of the game soundtrack, and many more. Fans of horror games should prepare for a breathtaking experience because a free PC demo will be available as part of Steam Next Fest in October. However, this is not the first chance to get your hands on the game’s unreal Sanity Effect feature and take on the terrifying monstrosities that await inside the depths of the Slavic underworld because the game is available to playtest for free during Early Access via Discord server.

[previewyoutube=vixGafn2KJw;full][/previewyoutube]

Here are a few details from the Code Alkonost showcase presentation:
 

 The main protagonist of Code Alkonost is a young Slavic girl who discovers her abilities and life purpose during her journey into the underworld. The game protagonist has no weapons or way to fight back. During her progress, she will reach that point of maturity where her body is abruptly changing and she will develop the confidence to make her own decisions, and resist attempts by unwanted creatures to take her soul and control over her own body.
 Immerse yourself inside dynamic and atmospheric environments, and learn how to use witchcraft to protect yourself from enemies. Learn about game characters and solve puzzles to progress further.
 Code Alkonost features unique content from an ethnographic museum and famous locations never seen in any game before. Scanned face models and voiceovers of real word actors that will provide a breathtaking cinematic experience developed using novel state-of-the-art technologies.
 Professional performers will provide voice-overs for video game creatures and create the feeling that someone is watching you.
 The Sanity Effect can impact the game's overall audiovisual experience by adding tension and fear inside the game environment. For an immersive experience and psychological effects, we use Unreal Engine 5.
 Playtester statement: Code Alkonost is an amazing experience, I wasn't aware that I am playing an indie video game, the unique gameplay and sanity effect is breathtaking and unpredictable, this product has many innovative features for horror gamers. 

 
For more details check the showcase video presentation  and provide a feedback via super quick survey.

For more information, visit Code Alkonost website, follow the title on Facebook, Twitch, Instagram, and YouTube, support developers on Patreon and Ko-Fi, and join the community on Discord. Check out the latest screenshots from the Unreal Engine 5 playtest build via Steam page. Players can look forward to a fully fleshed-out Code Alkonost experience when the first chapter of the game launches during Q1 2023.
